name: Presslyte – Front End Text Editor
author: Presslyte

sections.description:
Presslyte is a front end editor for making quick text changes on your existing WordPress website. Fix a typo, update business hours or change a heading directly on the page. Click supported highlighted text, type your change, preview and save.

Edit supported native WordPress paragraphs, headings and lists, plus supported static text in standard, page-owned Elementor Heading and Text Editor widgets. Layout settings, forms, navigation and unsupported content stay protected.

Included in Free

  • On-page editing of supported native WordPress paragraphs, headings and list text.
  • Static wording in standard, page-owned Elementor Heading and Text Editor widgets.
  • Preview, Save and optional autosave.
  • Typing Undo and Redo, saved History and local recovery.
  • Page navigation and favorite pages.
  • Local spelling suggestions and Find on this page.
  • Guided first-edit help, written guides and video tutorial links.

Presslyte Free works without a Presslyte account or license key. There is no editing quota. Your WordPress permissions control who can edit.

A clear editing boundary

Presslyte highlights text only when it can verify the saved WordPress or supported Elementor text source. Choose a highlighted paragraph, heading or list item to begin. Page structure, forms, dynamic output, code and existing link destinations stay protected.

Use a compatible theme, supported native WordPress blocks, or supported standard Elementor text widgets. Preview your wording and check the saved page; longer text can naturally change wrapping and page height.

Privacy and external services

Editing and the built-in introduction do not require external services. Presslyte stores local editor preferences, recovery drafts, saved versions and editor attribution. WordPress privacy export and erasure tools are supported; erasure anonymizes attribution while preserving shared page content and recovery history.

The Learn area opens written guides at https://presslyte.com/product-updates/ and video tutorials at https://presslyte.com/tutorials/ only when selected. Presslyte does not fetch a learning feed, load remote lesson thumbnails or schedule lesson updates. See https://presslyte.com/privacy/ for the destination privacy policy.

The optional compatibility-help and support links open https://presslyte.com/support/ in a new tab only when selected. Opening them does not automatically send your site URL, content or diagnostic details. You choose what to share and submit on that website.

Optional testing feedback is disabled by default. When an administrator enables it, sending the feedback form uses the site’s WordPress mail service to send the entered message, plugin version and optional reply email to support@presslyte.com. Sending requires an explicit user action.

Deactivation retains content and recovery records. Deleting the plugin retains settings and recovery history by default. The explicit erase-on-uninstall setting removes Free editor settings and recovery history while leaving published page content and stored mapped text intact.
sections.installation:
1. Install Presslyte through Plugins > Add New, or upload the presslyte folder to your WordPress plugins directory.
  2. Activate Presslyte.
  3. Open Presslyte in your WordPress dashboard and choose a page.
  4. Select highlighted supported text, make a change, preview and save.
  5. Check the refreshed page. Keep your normal site backup alongside Presslyte History.
sections.faq:
What can I edit?

Supported native WordPress paragraph, heading and list text, plus static wording in standard Elementor Heading and Text Editor widgets that Presslyte highlights on the page. Highlighting means Presslyte has verified the saved text source for that editing session.

Does Free work with Elementor?

Yes, for supported static text in standard Heading and Text Editor widgets saved directly on the page. Text Editor paragraphs, headings and list items are supported when their source can be verified. Dynamic content, shared templates, nested or third-party widgets, media and layout settings are outside this support. Ambiguous text stays read-only.

Do I need an account or license key?

No. Presslyte Free uses your existing WordPress permissions and has no editing quota.

Is Presslyte a page builder?

No. It handles supported wording changes on an existing page. Keep page structure and design in the WordPress tools that manage them.

Can I preview a change?

Yes. Select Preview to check your wording. The toolbar’s Hide button also clears the editing marks while keeping the controls available.

Will my wording stay after a refresh?

A successful Save stores supported text in WordPress and refreshes the page with the persisted result. Check the page after saving.

Can I undo or recover an edit?

Use Undo and Redo while typing. History and the available recovery controls help you find saved versions and recover supported changes. Keep a normal site backup too.

Does spelling check change text automatically?

No. The local spelling tool offers suggestions for you to review.

Who can edit?

Users must have the required WordPress permissions for the content. Presslyte keeps server-side permission and source checks in place.

Where can I find help?

Use Help in the toolbar for the guided first edit, or open the written guides and video tutorials in Learn. For a different or custom theme, choose Request theme compatibility help in the dashboard or editor Settings. You can ask us to review your setup without a Presslyte account or license.

Can I help translate Presslyte?

Yes. Help translate Presslyte on WordPress.org. Language availability depends on translations approved by the WordPress community. Translation support covers the plugin interface; it does not translate your page content.
sections.changelog:
1.1.17

  • Clarify the plugin name, short description, introductory wording and editing tags in the WordPress.org listing.
  • Preserve existing editing behavior, supported content boundaries and recovery tools.

1.1.16

  • Show the editor for supported standard Elementor Heading and Text Editor wording.
  • Verify page-owned widget identities and preserve layout settings and existing link destinations.
  • Add optional theme compatibility help and an explanatory support link on unsupported pages.

1.1.15

  • Clarify the directory name, summary and editing tags.
  • Make search, spelling, recovery, help and accessibility messages discoverable by WordPress translation tools.
  • Load interface translations for the shipped scripts and improve plural forms and translator context.
  • Keep language switching compatible with WordPress 5.8–6.0 and let longer toolbar labels wrap without changing the English layout.
  • Make the empty-text hint translatable and keep save status independent of English wording.
  • Add a link for community translation contributions.

1.1.14

  • Initial Presslyte Free release.
  • Edit supported native WordPress text directly on the page, preview and save.
  • Includes typing Undo and Redo, saved History, local recovery, page navigation and favorites.
  • Includes local spelling suggestions, Find on this page and guided help.
